# Repository Guidelines

## Agent bootstrap

Before changing files, read `.ai/architecture.yaml`, `.ai/rules/common.md`, `.ai/service.yaml`, `.ai/commands.yaml`, `docs/README.md`, the relevant `.ai/workflows/*` workflow, and affected contracts. Capture `git status --short` and `git diff`, then run the canonical policy command `./scripts/check-agent-policy.sh`; stop fail-closed if it fails. Code, migrations, tests, and repository-owned documents are authoritative.

## Architecture invariants

- `internal/domain` owns teacher types and ports; `internal/usecase` owns orchestration and deterministic pedagogy behavior; adapters own HTTP, PostgreSQL, NATS, and future approved service-client details.
- This service owns the logical `PersonalTeacher`, explainable teacher decisions, and teacher-owned assistance facts. Student knowledge, mastery, paths, sessions, attempts, and evidence projections remain owned by `ms-go-student`.
- `PersonalTeacher` contains teacher identity and behavior settings only. `StudentContext` is a bounded request snapshot, never a second student database.
- `TeacherSoul` is one-to-one with the same PersonalTeacher/student pair, has independent optimistic versioning, and contains only bounded identity/voice/relationship settings. Never use it as student memory or store mastery, evidence, history, code, or prompts in it.
- Deterministic teaching, hint, intervention, and mode policies must be tested before model generation. LLM providers and prompt execution remain behind use-case ports.
- Pedagogical methods implement the use-case `PedagogyMethod` port and are selected through the composition-root registry. TeacherOrchestrator must not switch on concrete methodologies; every plan and decision records method code/version and a method-neutral stage.
- Prompt, provider, and structured-output schemas are versioned contracts. Never persist or publish chain-of-thought, raw model reasoning, raw prompts, student code, private dialog history, or unrestricted model output.
- The Dialog consumer acknowledges only after `teacher_dialog_job` durably accepts the request or verifies an identical duplicate. General context uses only Student's bounded learner overview; lesson context remains durable blocked work until authoritative projections exist.
- The source `dialog.teacher.requested.event_id` is the generation and Dialog-append idempotency key. A generated response may exist only as private pending-delivery state and must be cleared after verified append.
- Deterministic `teacher-dialog-policy-v1` owns the help level and never permits a complete solution; the model formulates within that plan through confidential `teacher.response.v1` execution.
- Messaging uses a PostgreSQL transactional outbox, versioned envelope, stable event identity, and at-least-once delivery. Consumers must deduplicate.
- Consume `learning_action.closed` from `TASKANSWER_EVENTS` through the inbound `internal/transport/message/nats` contour. Correlation is the distinct action-cycle ID; invalid/version-mismatched payloads terminate and transient persistence failures retry.
- Consume bounded `learning.activity.interesting` observations from `LEARNING_ANALYTICS_EVENTS`; deterministic replaceable intervention policy owns speak versus silence, and proactive delivery is idempotent through the student's general Dialog.
- `teacher.assistance.observed` contains teacher-owned assistance only. It cannot assert task success, score, confidence, or mastery.
- Task-scoped `TeacherDecision` rows must carry `learning_action_id` and use it as `correlation_id`. Finalization aggregates only locally recorded teacher actions. Targetless actions are inbox-only and never invent observations.
- Transport layout is fail-closed: direct children of `internal/transport` are limited to `http`, `message`, `cli`, `websocket`, and `common`; direct children of `internal/transport/http` are limited to `api`, `admin`, and `private`.
- Public, admin, and private HTTP handlers and audience-specific helpers belong exclusively to `api/v1`, `admin/v1`, and `private` respectively. Routers must not import another contour's transport code.
- API/admin authentication is composed by the root router; each route applies its own explicit role allowlist. Private routes are unversioned under `/internal` and require the exact shared token.
- `internal/infrastructure` is outbound-only and fail-closed to the real paths declared in `.ai/architecture.yaml`; approved HTTP clients are `student`, `course`, `practice`, `dialog`, `aiprompt`, and `statistic`; `internal/adapters` is forbidden.
- `internal/domain` and `internal/usecase` must not import transport, infrastructure, chi, pgx, NATS, Zap, validators, or model-provider SDKs. Composition wiring belongs in `cmd/ms-go-teacher-agent/main.go`.
- Do not add direct knowledge-tree access or copy course content. Use approved versioned contracts and provider-neutral learning-target references.

## Verification and delivery

- Use `.ai/commands.yaml`. After edits, rerun `./scripts/check-agent-policy.sh` and every scope-relevant declared verification command. Report each exact command and exit status; failed, skipped, or missing required evidence forbids completion or review.
- HTTP, prompt, model-provider, teaching-policy, event, schema, integration, and migration changes require synchronized tests and owned contracts.
- Migrations, provider calls, services, deployments, and destructive stack commands require the approval stated in `.ai/commands.yaml`.
